{{family name hatnote|Pujol|Pons|lang=Catalan}}
'''Marc Pujol Pons''' (born 21 August 1982)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://int.soccerway.com/players/marc-pujol/55897/|title=Andorra - Marc Pujol - Profile with news, career statistics and history - Soccerway|website=int.soccerway.com}}</ref> is an [[Andorra]]n [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Midfielder|midfielder]] for [[Atlètic Club d'Escaldes|AC Escaldes]] in [[Andorra]]'s [[Primera Divisió]].

==Career==

He finished in third place at [[Preferent Territorial de Catalunya|Primera Catalana]] 2000–01, and promotion to [[Tercera División|Tercera division]] with [[FC Andorra|Andorra]]. He also finished in third place at [[Tercera División|Tercera division]] group 5 2002–03 with [[UE Sant Andreu|Sant Andreu]]. He later signed with the [[SCR Peña Deportiva|Peña Deportiva]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.periodicodeibiza.es/deportes/deporte-ibiza/2004/02/19/678591/inigo-y-pujol-con-hambre-de-exitos.html|title=Iñigo y Pujol, con hambre de éxitos|website=periodicodeibiza|date=19 February 2004 |language=es|accessdate=3 December 2024}}</ref>

Later on, Pujol achieved second place at Primera Territorial Catalana 2010–11 and promoted to Segona Catalana with [[FC Andorra|Andorra]]. He also attained second place at Segona Catalana 2011–12 and promoted to [[Preferent Territorial de Catalunya|Primera Catalana]] with [[FC Andorra|Andorra]]. He later won [[Andorra]]'s [[Primera Divisió]] 2013–14 with [[FC Santa Coloma]].

==International==
Pujol made his debut for [[Andorra national football team|Andorra]] in a friendly game against [[Albania national football team|Albania]] on 6 February 2000, becoming at 17 years and 5 months his country’s youngest player, beating [[Ildefons Lima|Ildefons Lima’s]] record.<ref> {{cite web |title=Albania vs Andorra |url=https://www.national-football-teams.com/matches/report/23337/Albania_Andorra.html |website=National Football Teams |access-date=17 November 2024}}</ref> His record was eventually beaten by [[Iván Lorenzo]] in 2003 and then [[Sergi Moreno]] in 2004. Pujol played in a match against [[England national football team|England]] at [[Old Trafford]] held on 2 September 2006 but had to withdraw shortly after the start of the second half due to a leg injury after a tangle with [[Ashley Cole]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/history/news/0254-0d7b8c80d313-d43f868b8d22-1000--england-ease-to-winning-start/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131016103416/http://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/season=2008/matches/round=2241/match=83917/postmatch/report/index.html#england+ease+winning+start|archive-date=16 October 2013|title=England ease to winning start|url-status=live|date=2 September 2006}}</ref>

On 12 October 2021, Pujol scored his fourth goal for Andorra during a [[2022 FIFA World Cup qualification – UEFA Group I|2022 FIFA World Cup qualification game]] against [[San Marino national football team|San Marino]], becoming at 39 years and 1 months their oldest-ever goalscorer as well as [[UEFA]]'s oldest [[FIFA World Cup qualification]] goalscorer, though the latter record was beaten on 7 June 2025 by Bosnian [[Edin Džeko]].<ref>{{cite web |title=San Marino 0-3 Andorra |url=https://www.uefa.com/european-qualifiers/match/2030959--san-marino-vs-andorra/ |website=UEFA |access-date=17 November 2024}}</ref> Three years later, on 13 October 2024, he scored his fifth goal for Andorra in a friendly, again against San Marino, and in doing so at the age of 42 years and 53 days, he became the oldest European international goalscorer, breaking a 68-year-old record set by [[Stanley Matthews]] in 1956, at 41 years and 248 days.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://iffhs.com/en/news/marc-pujol-in-history-3923 |title=Marc Pujol beat Stanley Matthews’s record! |website=www.iffhs.com |date=14 October 2024 |access-date=11 June 2025 }}</ref>

He retired from the Andorra national team at the age of 43 on 4 June 2026.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.alto.ad/sports/andorra-marc-pujol-farewell-international-260603 |title=Marc Pujol Set for Farewell 124th Cap in Andorra's Friendly vs Liechtenstein |publisher=alto.ad |date=4 June 2026 }}</ref>
